summary: Three findings: one high-severity overgeneralization of valuation-ring local freeness, and two medium-severity library/ownership errors. The pinned library already supplies symmetric monoidal functors and monoidal natural transformations. Four general K-theory inputs are assigned to the low-degree determinant route despite their existing general/scheme K-theory owners. All 311 missing items have exactly one route, the 29 distinct named destination stages resolve, and the internal prerequisite graph is acyclic. These findings do not refute the paper's projectivity theorem.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17.result.json: item PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/cited-rg-flat-fp-algebra-free (route 1); companion reader's current extraction summary
findings.claim: The item asserts that flatness and finite presentation over a rank-one valuation ring make the structure sheaf locally a free module over that ring. This is false even for a complete henselian valuation ring. It omits the closed-fibre/local-henselian scope of the cited corollary and the properness available in Bhatt–Scholze's application.
findings.evidence: BS17 arXiv v3 p. 26, proof of Theorem 6.13, takes X_0 to be a 'proper flat and reduced model' before invoking RG71, Corollary 3.3.13. RG71 I.3.3.13, printed p. 23, assumes a finitely presented pointed map (X,x)→(S,s), a finitely presented sheaf flat at x, and (S,s) local henselian; it supplies an affine neighbourhood of x with free sections over Gamma(S,O_S). Counterexample to the extracted statement: for any nonfield rank-one valuation ring V and 0≠t in its maximal ideal, K=Frac(V)=V[1/t] is the finitely presented flat V-algebra V[T]/(tT−1). The scheme Spec K has one point, but its nonzero section module K is not free over V: K/tK=0, whereas a nonzero free V-module has nonzero quotient modulo t. This also works for perfect valuation rings with algebraically closed complete fraction field.
findings.fix: Replace the title and statement by the actual pointed local-henselian corollary, or its sufficient application: a proper flat finitely presented scheme over a henselian valuation ring admits an affine open cover whose section rings are free V-modules, with rank possibly infinite. Explain that the corollary first covers the closed fibre and properness makes that open cover cover X_0: a nonempty closed complement would have closed nonempty image in the local base, hence meet its closed point. Retain the paper's complete/algebraically closed valuation setting and the other hypotheses used separately in the Hom calculation. Keep route 1; do not generalize to arbitrary flat finitely presented V-algebras. Record Spec V[1/t] as a counterexample in the correction.

findings.claim: The ordinary symmetric monoidal functor and monoidal natural transformation of appendix section 12 are marked missing and routed as new work. Both are already supplied by the pinned Mathlib library. L35 credits symmetric categories, but does not repair this item's separate missing status.
findings.evidence: At Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean:389 defines CategoryTheory.Functor.Monoidal with inverse lax/oplax unit and tensor constraints; lines 405 and 411 provide the corresponding isomorphisms. Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Braided/Basic.lean:531 defines CategoryTheory.Functor.Braided extending Monoidal and LaxBraided; the latter's equation at lines 385–388 is precisely compatibility with braiding. Between SymmetricCategory instances this is a symmetric monoidal functor. Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/NaturalTransformation.lean:46 defines CategoryTheory.NatTrans.IsMonoidal with the unit and tensor compatibility equations. BS17 p. 54 recalls these ordinary categorical notions before passing to their K-theory.
findings.fix: Mark the item library and cite Functor.Braided (with SymmetricCategory source and target), Functor.Monoidal and NatTrans.IsMonoidal at the pin; split the two notions only if that improves the inventory. Remove it from route 12's missing-work list, update totals and the reader, and make the Segal/K-theory constructions consume these existing definitions. Keep the higher coherent constructions and the inherited symmetric monoidal structure on Core as separate obligations unless independently verified.

findings.claim: Four general K-theory suppliers are assigned as missing source work to KTheoryLowDegrees Z.3/U.3/U.6, although their mathematics belongs to the already identified general/scheme K-theory owners. These are not merely determinant-specific consequences: they define whole support spectra and assert spectrum-level additivity, K/G comparison and localization. Route 10 imports the correct owners in prose but its item assignments still send their construction to the determinant consumer.
findings.evidence: BS17 section 5, pp. 18–19, uses general K-theory additivity and, in the proof of Theorem 5.5, the regular K=G comparison and the two localization sequences. At atlas a7560b3, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction expressly requires additivity for the S-construction; SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.3 defines support K-theory from complexes acyclic off Z and its localization fibre sequence; S.2 owns the Cartan K→G comparison, including regular noetherian finite-dimensional cases; GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.3 owns Quillen localization for Serre quotients. In contrast, Z.3 constructs degree-zero tensor/exterior/determinant operations, U.3 the stable determinant and SK1, and U.6 the low-degree homotopy comparison. The extraction's route 9 already assigns scheme/support K-theory to S.2/S.3, and route 11 already identifies K.3/K.4.
findings.fix: Reassign these supplier items to routes 9/11 and their exact existing stages, leaving determinant-specific consequences in route 10 with explicit imports. Mark the covered support construction and localization/additivity results planned rather than missing; split the paired K/G localization item if necessary to express its two suppliers. For K=G, compare its full regular-noetherian scope with S.2's finite-dimensional promise: retain any genuinely broader extension as a source addition to S.2, not as low-degree determinant work. Update the reader and counts and preserve one owner for each supplier. Do not delete the extraction items or demand a recursive proof audit of TT90/Quillen.
